items.title: There's a ceasefire in Iran but the war's ripples are still hitting millions
items.description: It has been more than two months since the US and Israel launched strikes in Iran. But the impact of the conflict continues globally.

items.title: Liberal senator speaks out against Taylor's budget reply
items.description: Senator Andrew McLachlan raises concerns over Angus Taylor's use of the term "mass immigration" and plan to push tax-paying migrants off welfare benefits.

items.title: Gaza families are still unable to bury dead trapped under rubble
items.description: The families of Palestinians believed to be trapped under the rubble of collapsed buildings want to bury their dead.

items.title: Tax is a great motivator but will Labor's changes fix Australia's housing mess?
items.description: The Albanese government and the opposition both want to turn back the clock on the Australian tax system.

items.title: How some countries dodged interest rate rises for years
items.description: As Australians pay more on their mortgages, some countries have had no rise in their interest rate in recent years. So what's going on?

items.title: 'Boomer bashing': Are cuts to private health rebates addressing generational or wealth inequality?
items.description: The federal government plans to reduce private health insurance rebates for older Australians, a move one advocate fears could "tip many over the edge".

items.title: Ex-Labor powerbroker's warning amid NDIS cuts
items.description: A former NSW Labor powerbroker and state disability minister pivotal in advocating for the establishment of the NDIS has warned against rushing through sweeping changes to the scheme.

items.title: 'Devoted father and gentleman': Tributes flow for shark attack victim
items.description: The wife of a 38-year-old Perth man who died in a shark attack off the coast of Rottnest Island in Western Australia on Saturday describes him as a devoted father and avid spearfisherman.

items.title: Push for Australia to extract helium as Iran war impacts global supply
items.description: Helium is needed in health care and to make microchips and semiconductors, but the Middle East war has affected supply. Some think it is an opportunity for Australia's gas industry.

items.title: UAE slams 'dangerous escalation' after drone hits near nuclear plant
items.description: Abu Dhabi officials say radiation levels are normal and there was no damage to the plant, but authorities are now working to determine who carried out the attack.

items.title: The $10b offer Dave Hughes would 'hand on heart' turn down
items.description: Comedian Dave Hughes spoke to The Assembly about why he quit alcohol at 22, being "addicted to work" and the type of dad he's trying to be for his three kids.

items.title: Ukraine launches massive drone wave against Russia, killing four
items.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the attacks were justified as "responses to Russia's prolongation of the war and its attacks on our cities and communities", two days after Russian strikes on Kyiv killed 24.

items.title: WHO declares Ebola outbreak an 'emergency of international concern'
items.description: At least 80 people have died in what the World Health Organization says potentially could be a "much larger outbreak than what is currently being detected and reported".

items.title: Protesters march at Nakba Day rallies around Australia
items.description: Crowds gather at rallies around the country to commemorate the anniversary of the Nakba, a day that recognises the mass displacement of Palestinians in 1948.

items.title: The science behind why break-ups are so difficult, even when you want to
items.description: It's not just practical and emotional reasons that get in the way of executing a break-up. There are many ways your brain is making you want to stay.

items.title: Quiz: It's history time! Where was Pac-Man first released?
items.description: In what year did John Howard become a federal MP? And which country got to play Pac-Man first? Test yourself in this week's history quiz.

items.title: How Pokémon cards are fuelling crime in Melbourne
items.description: Rare Pokémon cards can sell for hundreds or even thousands of dollars, with a record sale of one Pikachu card going for over $22 million earlier this year.

items.title: You could hear a pin drop when Rob revealed why he fought a fire tax
items.description: Every time farmer and volunteer firefighter Rob Armstrong gets a call to battle a bushfire, something inside says not to do it. But he goes anyway. He knows what it's like to be trapped in the flames and rescued by volunteers.

items.title: Harley heroics lift Eagles to stunning upset win over Giants
items.description: West Coast surges to a third victory of the season, defeating GWS by 17 points while St Kilda and Fremantle also enjoy Sunday wins.

items.title: Blues suffer Origin blow, Ponga will 'play anywhere' for Maroons
items.description: NSW has been dealt a State of Origin blow ahead of the Blues' team announcement on Monday, with Latrell Mitchell ruling himself out of Game I selection.

items.title: Sydney lawyer was stressed out by her mortgage so she sold up and bought a van
items.description: Phoebe Macdougall says she hated living with a mortgage, so she is trying van life instead.

items.title: Treasurer stands by CGT changes affecting shares and crypto
items.description: Jim Chalmers says it is better for young people to invest based on economic rather than tax outcomes, and argued they can still access negative gearing by buying up new homes.

items.title: Labor claims victory in Queensland's Stafford by-election
items.description: Labor candidate Luke Richmond claims victory over the LNP's Fiona Hammond in a tight race in the north Brisbane electorate of Stafford.

items.title: Qantas plane diverted after passenger allegedly bites flight attendant
items.description: Fellow passengers are believed to have assisted after a flight attendant was allegedly bitten on plane travelling between Melbourne and the US, with the plane diverted to Tahiti.

items.title: AI psychosis is on the rise and experts are sounding the alarm
items.description: Rodrigues thought an AI chatbot could help him escape poverty and build wealth. Instead, he became trapped in a spiral of delusion and dependence.
